facts.claim: More than 50 airlines operate the Boeing 787-9 and the overwhelming majority stop at business class; nothing about the airframe requires or prevents a first class cabin.
British Airways fits eight first class seats in a 1-2-1 herringbone across two rows on its 787-9; it offers first class on the 777, 787-9, 787-10 and A380, but not on the A350-1000 or the 787-8.
Etihad Airways operates four distinct 787-9 configurations, only one of which includes first class; that three-class layout carries eight first class suites in rows one and two.

Head for Points found United Airlines carrying 99 premium seats on its 787-9, ahead of Japan Airlines at 87 and British Airways at 85; United sells no first class, reaching the figure with 64 Polaris suites including eight Polaris Studios plus 35 Premium Plus seats.

British Airways announced a full A380 retrofit on October 5, 2026: the 2013 layout carried 14 First, 97 Club World, 55 World Traveller Plus and 303 World Traveller (469 seats); the 2026 layout carries 12 First, 106 Club Suites, 84 World Traveller Plus and 215 World Traveller (417 seats), taking the premium ratio from 35% to 48%.

Etihad offers no dedicated premium economy cabin; Head for Points put its A380 premium ratio at 16% against British Airways' 48%, and Prince of Travel found its first class deployed on four routes — Abu Dhabi to Casablanca, Geneva, London and Washington — all operated by the 787-9.

zh.title: 為何有些787-9有頭等艙、有些只到商務艙：英航8席與聯合99個高級座位的算盤
zh.summary: 全球50多家航空公司營運787-9，絕大多數只設商務艙；頭等艙的有無不是機身特性，而是航空公司對機頭空間的取捨。英航787-9設8個頭等座位，聯合航空則以64間北極星套房與35個豪華經濟艙湊出99個高級座位，成為全機型之最。
body: 波音787-9在全球由50多家航空公司營運，絕大多數只設商務艙，沒有頭等艙。這不是機身的限制：沒有任何設計要求787-9必須設頭等艙，也沒有任何設計阻止航空公司設置；頭等艙的有無，取決於航空公司為該機型選定的客艙配置，甚至同一家航空公司、同一機型也會因飛機而異。英航787-9設有8個頭等座位，以1-2-1人字形排列於兩個排數；阿提哈德航空則有四種不同的787-9配置，只有其中一種設頭等艙。

最能說明趨勢的數字來自座位數統計。據Head for Points統計，聯合航空787-9的高級座位達99個，居全機型之冠，其次為日本航空87個、英航85個；聯合航空完全不賣頭等艙，而是以64間北極星套房——其中8間為加大的北極星工作室（Polaris Studio）——加上35個豪華經濟艙（Premium Plus）達到這個數字。北極星工作室比標準北極星套房大25%，配備27吋（68.58公分）4K OLED螢幕、額外貴賓座、專屬主菜與魚子醬服務，須在北極星票價之外另付選位費，等於是以頭等艙產品放在商務艙內銷售。英航A380改裝計畫則在同一機型內呈現相同方向：2026年10月5日公布的改裝方案將頭等艙由14席減至12席，商務艙由97席增至106席，豪華經濟艙由55席增至84席，經濟艙由303席減至215席，總座位由469席降至417席，高級座位占比由35%升至48%，為所有A380營運商最高。

頭等艙正在收縮，原因不在需求消失，而在空間報酬。頭等艙占用機頭最值錢的地板面積、服務標準最昂貴、客源卻是各艙等中最少的；對787-9這類比777或A380更小的廣體機而言，這塊空間按比例更珍貴。商務艙如今已吸收頭等艙過去的賣點：隱私門、直通走道、封閉套房與大螢幕早已是具競爭力商務艙的標配；豪華經濟艙則吸納願意多付錢、但不到商務艙票價的旅客。阿提哈德航空的例子顯示反向操作也未必有利：該公司不設專屬豪華經濟艙，A380高級座位占比僅16%，遠低於英航的48%，儘管其上層甲板設有空中官邸（The Residence）與頭等艙公寓。據Prince of Travel統計，阿提哈德頭等艙實際上僅部署於阿布達比往返卡薩布蘭卡、日內瓦、倫敦與華盛頓四條航線，且皆由787-9執飛；該媒體記者搭乘阿提哈德787-9由馬累前往阿布達比時，執飛的飛機根本沒有頭等艙。

en.title: Why some Boeing 787-9s offer first class while others stop at business: BA's eight seats vs United's 99 premium seats
en.summary: More than 50 airlines fly the Boeing 787-9 and the overwhelming majority stop at business class. Whether a 787-9 has first class is a configuration decision, not an aircraft property: British Airways fits eight first class seats, while United Airlines reaches 99 premium seats — the most of any operator — without selling first class at all.
body: More than 50 airlines operate the Boeing 787-9 Dreamliner, and the overwhelming majority stop at business class. Nothing about the airframe requires a first class cabin or prevents one, which makes its presence a configuration decision rather than an aircraft property. British Airways is the most prominent operator fitting first class to the type: its 787-9 carries eight first class seats arranged in a 1-2-1 herringbone layout across two rows. Etihad Airways is the other notable case, operating four distinct 787-9 configurations, only one of which includes first class — a three-class layout carrying eight first class suites in rows one and two, with the suites alternating forward- and rearward-facing.

The more revealing figure is where the premium seats went instead. Head for Points found United Airlines carrying 99 premium seats on its 787-9, more than any other operator of the type, ahead of Japan Airlines at 87 and British Airways at 85. United sells no first class at all: it reaches that number through 64 Polaris suites, including eight enlarged Polaris Studios, plus 35 Premium Plus seats in a 222-seat aircraft. The Studio suites are 25% larger than standard Polaris and carry a 27-inch (68.58 cm) 4K OLED screen, an additional ottoman seat, exclusive entree options and Ossetra caviar service, sold through an additional seat selection fee on top of a Polaris booking — a first class product priced inside a business class cabin. British Airways' A380 retrofit shows the same shift inside one aircraft: announced on October 5, 2026, it cuts first class from 14 seats to 12 while raising business from 97 to 106 and premium economy from 55 to 84, with economy falling from 303 to 215. The aircraft loses 52 seats overall while gaining 36 premium seats, taking its premium ratio from 35% to 48%, the highest of any A380 operator.

First class is contracting because the floor space it occupies earns more as business and premium economy seating. First class consumes prime floor space at the front of the aircraft, demands the most expensive service standard onboard, and sells to the smallest pool of passengers of any cabin — and on a 787-9, which is smaller than a 777 or A380, that floor space is proportionally more valuable still. Business class has absorbed most of what first class used to offer: privacy doors, direct aisle access, enclosed suites and large personal screens were first class differentiators a decade ago and are now standard in competitive business cabins. Premium economy captures passengers who will pay above an economy fare but not a business one. Etihad shows what happens when an airline retains first class and skips premium economy entirely: the carrier offers no dedicated premium economy cabin, and Head for Points identified that absence as a significant reason its A380 premium ratio sits at 16% against British Airways' 48%, despite Etihad dedicating substantial upper deck space to The Residence and First Class Apartments. Prince of Travel found Etihad's first class deployment narrow in practice, available on four routes connecting Abu Dhabi with Casablanca, Geneva, London and Washington, all operated by the 787-9; the reviewers flew Etihad 787-9s on both legs of a trip and found the Male to Abu Dhabi sector had no first class cabin at all.
